description: We are building Project A.E.G.I.S., an autonomous health monitoring, emergency triage, and crew readiness web platform for Moon and Mars missions using real NASA OSDR & LOLA data. I'm an AI/ML & Data Science engineer with a ready backend/ML pipeline. Looking for a Frontend developer (React/Next.js) or UI/UX & Pitch contributor to build a Global Top-10 winning demo together!
summary: On long missions, astronauts can't wait 20 minutes for a doctor's reply, and an unnoticed fall, muscle ischemia or cardiac event can end an EVA. A.E.G.I.S. (Autonomous EVA Guidance & Integrated Survival) is an offline-capable health-monitoring software that turns wearable biosignals into one clear action in three modes: EVA safety with a walk-back limit adjusted for terrain, step-by-step emergency guidance for non-physicians with built-in safety locks, and an evening check that catches hidden exhaustion. Prototype validated on NASA OSDR and public physiological datasets; designed to align with NASA-STD-3001.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

Our Project:

  • Prevents crises during spacewalks (Mode 1 · EVA): tracks leg muscle fatigue and oxygen consumption while accounting for actual crater slope, calculates the "point of no return" countdown (Walk-Back Limit) in advance, and displays a short command on the visor and wrist display.
  • Guides a non-physician step-by-step in an emergency (Mode 2 · Emergency): automatically activates emergency triage when an alarm is triggered or a fall occurs—identifies the diagnosis using 4 visual symptom cards and voice, strictly blocks dangerous mistakes (such as prohibiting nitroglycerin when blood pressure is low, BP < 90), reads out step-by-step first aid instructions, and queues a report for Flight Surgeons on Earth.
  • Catches hidden exhaustion in the evening (Mode 3 · Evening): compares the astronaut's self-assessment against actual biometrics (Mismatch detector), assigns recovery quests, monitors 6 body systems via a clickable body figure, and prepares a summary for the commander to adjust the schedule.

What benefits does it have?

  • All-in-One Base Layer: Combines fragmented devices (watches, shirts, clips, and lab gear) into a single unified garment worn underneath a lunar spacesuit.
  • Real-Time EVA Safety (catching muscle ischemia or balance loss mid-walk).
  • Continuous Muscle & Gait Tracking: Uses sEMG, NIRS, and IMU tracking continuously during lunar labor to prevent falls and exhaustion.
  • Passive Bone & Blood Pressure Tracking: Uses 14-day algorithmic bone-load trend analysis and continuous, cuffless optical blood pressure instead of heavy DEXA scanners and inflatable cuffs.

Our challenge is to help astronauts monitor their health, understand their health status, and respond to potential health problems more easily.

In a medical emergency, astronauts must manage critical conditions without immediate medical assistance.


Astronauts on long-duration missions often face problems such as:

  • Heart muscle weakening and irregular heartbeats.
  • Dizziness, nausea, disorientation and impaired coordination.
  • Low blood oxygen and carbon dioxide buildup.
  • Muscle loss, weakness and fatigue.
  • Bone density loss and increased fracture risk.
  • Reduced blood volume, blood clots and blood pressure changes.

There's limited medical support in space, no doctors on board and communication from earth is delayed.

Future vision

  • Connecting to real spacesuit sensors: transitioning the system from test data directly to real biometric base layers and the life support systems of new lunar spacesuits (AxEMU).
  • Testing on real AR visors and sleeve displays: checking how readable the prompts are on the helmet glass and how convenient it is to control the system in thick gloves or by voice.
  • Fully autonomous AI for missions to Mars: running an embedded neural network directly on the lunar base or spacecraft computer so the crew receives medical recommendations even during a complete loss of communication with Earth.

Coding languages:
TypeScript, Python, JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3

Tools, Software & Services:
Next.js, React, FastAPI, LightGBM, Scikit-learn, WebSockets, Three.js, Vosk WebAssembly, Framer Motion, Vitest, Git, GitHub

Personal computers , Mobile smartphones
